# PB-04 isolated rooted admission experiment

Status: experimental, no production schema or Storage API change. PB-04 remains
open. This is a no-consumer/no-waiter admission experiment, not a new supported
operating envelope, protected storage format or production owner implementation.

The production projection increment is separately committed as
`7e669e179e6cc726185ac80627a6bdca146944f1`. Prototype examples and tables are isolated.

## Complete canonical dependency certificate

The experiment calls the existing `Engine::admit_event_in_epoch`, followed by its
existing `indexes::sync` and transaction checks. It does not implement a second
event-transition engine. The partial State is an isolated planner input, never
returned by a public Storage.load implementation. The following certificate must
be established from one authoritative rooted state before the call:

| State source | Read or proof | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| artifacts | Read all installed artifacts, in canonical map order | find_event and sensitive event/asynchronous completion checks scan them. Cost is O(A), not constant in catalog size. |
| catalog_revision, sequence | Read exact scalars | AcceptedEvent metadata and global sequence allocation. |
| retention.policy | Read full policy | Event expiry computation uses replay duration. |
| retention.producer_epochs | Point read/absence for authenticated producer | Exact epoch fence, absent means canonical default zero. |
| retention.event_tombstones | Point read/absence for exact canonical event key | Tombstone conflict and expired identity refusal. |
| events | Point read/absence for exact event key | Exact duplicate/content/expiry behavior. Existing event destinations are read with that event. |
| retention.event_expires_at_ms | Point read/absence for event key | Existing event replay deadline. |
| retention.event_epochs | Point read/absence for event key | Expected previous value for canonical insertion patch. |
| indexes.initialized | Prove true | Otherwise canonical transaction rebuild reads the full source state. |
| indexes.dirty_runs, dirty_intents | Prove empty | Otherwise sync can read and rewrite omitted runs/intents. |
| indexes.triggers | Prove absent/empty at trigger_key(contract,scope) | Any relevant consumer requires explicit full-reference fallback. Thus bindings/dependencies/admission protection branches cannot execute. |
| indexes.waiters | Prove absent/empty at full correlation key and EACH field key | Any relevant waiter requires fallback. Thus wake, run scheduling, completion_ready and dirty source mutations cannot execute. |
| indexes.events | Exact group existence/path proofs for those correlation keys | New sequence leaves are merged without erasing retained correlation history. A conflicting old leaf refuses the patch. |
| indexes.event_memberships | Exact event-key value/absence | Canonical index_event overwrite must not silently replace omitted data. |
| runs, events, receipts quota counts | Root-authenticated subtree entry/array counts | Planner-local empty collections are NOT the full namespace quota. |
| queued destination count | Genesis full audit proves zero; supported lineage cannot create destinations | Any other mutator requires reference fallback; no generic full-CAS writer is exposed by the prototype. This is deliberately limited. |
| canonical namespace bytes | Exact authenticated root length after patch | Same canonical State byte quota, including all omitted history. |

The remaining top-level fields are **omitted**, not falsely proved empty:
`catalog_history`, `catalog_history_at_ms`, `execution_denied`,
`authority_revocations`, `recovery_requests`, `bindings`, `runs`, `receipts`,
`intents`, `waits`, `budgets`. The no-consumer/no-waiter/empty-dirty certificate
excludes every canonical branch that could read them, except the independently
enforced full-root quota counts. The planner reads all artifacts for the protection
predicate even though protection_available is false in this unprotected experiment.

Remaining retention members (`last_gc_at_ms`, `expired_correlations`,
`artifact_disposals`, `disposals`, `gc_cursor`) are not used by this transition.
All other runtime-index members remain untouched: no relevant waiters means
index_event only inserts correlation sequence membership; empty dirty sets make
sync a no-op. MemoryStorage's artifact-removal check sees the complete unchanged
artifact set, so it does not enter removal/reference scans. Serialized State,
retention and index field sets have explicit tripwires: a schema addition requires
another dependency review. These tripwires supplement the source audit; they do
not prove future code changes preserve the read set by themselves.

## One authority and absence

An isolated root row is locked with `SELECT FOR UPDATE`, checked against one fixed
owner and updated with an expected revision predicate. Immutable content-addressed
nodes and the root publish in one PostgreSQL transaction. This demonstrates atomic
publication, not production incarnation/lease/authority qualification. A real
adapter must integrate the existing authoritative namespace ownership fencing.
The root row is trusted under that owner boundary; hash nodes do not authenticate
an arbitrary malicious replacement of the authoritative root itself.

Every object is an immutable AVL key map. Its node contains canonical key/value
and child references, subtree entry count, height and exact canonical byte
contribution. A reader freshly verifies stored bytes, their hash, canonical form,
and the expected metadata. Lookup absence is established by traversing those
verified edges to a missing child, not by trusting a SQL index or missing SQL row.
A missing referenced node fails. Genesis additionally derives trigger/waiter maps
from the full canonical source state and refuses drift; supported later admissions
preserve those source/index invariants. A generic corrupt full-State importer is
not an admissible prototype writer.

The point-read variant performs one query per uncached node. The batched variant
fetches independent required frontier nodes with one bounded `hash=ANY` query per
round, then verifies every returned byte and expected edge locally. Catalog
subtrees are fetched in bounded breadth-first frontiers because canonical event
validation requires all installed artifacts. Neither variant caches across a
transaction. Both variants use the same planner, patcher, tree representation,
workload, exact quotas and full-reference checks.

## Exact accounting and actual bounds

Scalars and opaque array leaves contribute their canonical encoded byte length.
An object contributes two braces, each canonical key length plus colon and child
length, and max(count-1,0) commas. AVL map nodes sum entry contributions; rotations
recompute authenticated ancestors. Changing a key cannot approximate its escaping
or digit width. Exact canonical full-state serialization is compared after every
measured event, outside measured latency. Arrays are opaque leaves; any existing
array edit, deletion, receipt compaction/offset change, consumer, waiter or dirty
source synchronization falls back. Receipt maintenance remains O(S/H) on the old
path, including all shifted offsets and changed decimal lengths.

For H retained records and bounded JSON depth, touched object paths cost O(log H)
node work per path plus all catalog A. There is no O(W) guarantee for a catalog
whose size grows with history. The mutable working set includes verified nodes,
new nodes, canonical planner artifacts and at most changed-record payloads;
full audit/differential verification intentionally materializes O(S) separately.
Prototype hard refusal bounds are 1,024-byte keys, AVL height below 64, at most
128 requested paths of depth 8, at most 512 proof rounds, 4,096 nodes per SQL
frontier, 256 subtree frontier rounds, 262,144 cached/pending nodes and 128 MiB
freshly fetched bytes. A single encoded node is capped at 16 MiB. These are
prototype refusal limits, not widened production namespace quotas. SQL/driver
allocation happens before local row-byte checks, so this is not a hard process
RSS or PostgreSQL resource guarantee. Pending cache/node bytes are not yet a
complete aggregate hard memory quota; production admission cannot claim them.
The experiment reports fetched/written node counts and bytes, wall latency,
physical database bytes and process maximum RSS.

## Integrity boundary, migration and compatibility

Admission validates touched nodes and all installed catalog bytes. It does not
scan unrelated run/receipt history on each admission. A deliberately corrupted
untouched receipt leaf may therefore allow unrelated planning, but the explicit
full audit and cold full reader must reject it. Newly staged duplicate addresses
are re-read and compared with exact bytes before publication; an existing corrupt
row cannot be hidden by address equality. This scope change would require explicit
production acceptance: the present full snapshot load detects all snapshot-byte
corruption per operation. No documentation promises both bounded working-set
access and a full scan of untouched history on every operation.

There is no production migration in this experiment. Future migration must acquire
exclusive authoritative ownership, verify the complete old snapshot/artifacts,
construct and audit the rooted state and exact counters, then atomically switch
an explicit version selector. Failure before switching leaves the old format
usable; after switching the complete new root must be usable. Retaining an old
snapshot that is not updated with new commits is not rollback. Reversion requires
an exclusive full verified materialization of the latest root and an atomic
selector swap. Old binaries must refuse the new selector. New code must preserve
public full load/CAS semantics by full materialization/rebuild (allowed O(S));
never return a partial State silently. Mixed namespaces, protected encryption,
key rotation, GC reachability/protection, crash recovery, ownership failover and
old/new caller concurrency remain production design/qualification gates, not
features of the synthetic plaintext tables.

## Frozen measurement results

The matched point and batched runs use identical frozen 53-file source inventories
and identical release binary bytes. Each executes 24 admissions at each history
0/32/128/512, with the unchanged PB02 five-artifact fixture, 128-byte string
payload, synchronous durable pinned PostgreSQL and the same namespace quotas.
Every event is compared with the full reference engine and exact serializer;
all 96 state hashes and canonical byte counts also match across both variants.
Both runs complete four fresh-connection full audits and 15 named correctness
checks. The checks additionally cover nonempty unrelated closed intents,
source-derived relevant waiter/consumer fallback, duplicate/conflict/expiry/epoch,
forged producer, dirty-index fallback, quota/transaction rollback, changed backing
bytes (including deduplication), untouched-history audit detection and canonical
escaping/delimiters/AVL rotations. No protected or production ownership behavior
is claimed by these checks.

| Retained histories | Point-read p95 ms | Batched p95 ms | Mean point SQL reads | Mean batched SQL reads | Mean proof bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 198.826 | 54.239 | 338.83 | 53.92 | 72,373 |
| 32 | 223.514 | 57.146 | 350.58 | 58.83 | 77,385 |
| 128 | 384.532 | 57.431 | 358.75 | 62.13 | 81,148 |
| 512 | 199.214 | 77.255 | 368.13 | 66.00 | 85,523 |

Every cell fails the unchanged 25 ms event budget. The point 128-history tail is
retained, not removed as an outlier. These are shared-host observations; varying
load means percentile ratios are not controlled speedup guarantees. Query counts
and verified proof bytes establish the mechanism: batching fetches the same fresh
proof nodes with fewer driver calls. They are driver API calls, not packet/wire
round-trip counts. The prototype still walks the whole required catalog and its
fine-grained object encoding; it has not removed all history/cost slopes or met
the CPU/ready-dispatch workloads. No broader PB04 performance acceptance follows.

The matched point process takes 51.47 s and reaches 91,180 KiB maximum RSS; batched
36.16 s and 90,780 KiB. These process totals include fixture creation, full audits
and correctness checks outside timed admissions. End database sizes are about
26.94/29.32 MB respectively; physical size includes fixture imports, dead tuples,
retained immutable path versions and development checks. It is not an amortized
per-event storage charge. No rooted GC or physical quota enforcement is qualified.
PostgreSQL is a fresh pinned 17.11 container with two CPUs, 1 GiB memory, 128 MiB
shared memory, fsync/synchronous_commit/full_page_writes enabled. The release
process runs on the shared host without its own CPU/memory cgroup. All exact
hardware, source/binary hashes, load averages, raw timings, process/database costs
and failures are retained in the companion JSON's evidence bundle.

The first development point run also completes 96 admissions plus four cold audits;
its slow per-node full audit lies outside admission timing. Its earlier source
archive is retained, along with failed fixture/harness development logs. The
matched runs batch their full audits outside timing so correctness is affordable;
this changes audit cost, not either admission variant's logical work or reference.
No failed performance cell is omitted and no limits are raised.

Production integration is **not approved** by this result. A further isolated
experiment could batch independent terminal value reads and/or verified recursive
path proofs more aggressively, still bound to the locked root. A production
working-set API additionally needs canonical planner extraction (this prototype
uses the existing engine on a certified partial view), real namespace ownership,
protected nodes/root context, migration/full-CAS compatibility, physical bounds
and GC. Those require a reviewed design and independent correctness/measurement;
PB04 remains open.
